paragraphs: R' Ada, son of R' Shimon, Megillah, chapter 1, halakhah 9.
Berakhot, chapter 2, at the end of halakhah 3, reads R' Idi, son of R' Shimon.
R' Yehudah, son of R' Shimon, Chullin 48a.[^1][^2]

notes.text: ה״ט is halakhah 9 and סה״ג contextually end of halakhah 3. Neither is a newly established modern reference or named corpus; Jerusalem Talmud remains suggested by form. Machine ארא/ה״מ/סה״נ differs from supplied אדא/ה״ט/סה״ג, without speculating that the source itself is OCR-derived.

מח.. is read 48a by period convention with an extra terminal stop, unlike machine מח.,; no new edition check. Ada/Idi and Yehudah remain separate patronymic attestations without a single-father identity. All seven title components, including each father-title, remain R'.
